690: The second unbeaten Triple Crown winner, with 7 G1 wins, and leading sire 11 years running - a modern legend who rewrote Japanese racing history. He won his debut with an astonishing 33.1 finish and took the Wakakoma S. by 5 lengths. In the Yayoi Sho he caught Admire Japan by a neck for his first graded win. In the Satsuki Sho he stumbled at the start yet still won by two and a half lengths, then took the Derby by 5 lengths in record-equaling time and the Kikuka Sho for an unbeaten Triple Crown. Beaten only by Heart's Cry in the Arima Kinen at 3, at 4 he won the Hanshin Daishoten, Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen with ease. He was 3rd in the Arc, later disqualified over a banned substance, but answered with overwhelming wins in the Japan Cup and Arima Kinen, retiring at the end of 2006 with 7 G1s, equal to the JRA record. At stud he sired Derby winner Deep Brillante and fillies' Triple Crown winner Gentildonna in his second crop, and was leading sire after just 3 crops. He died young in July 2019, at 17, and the Yayoi Sho was renamed the "Hochi Hai Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen" in his honor. He passed Sunday Silence for the most JRA wins as a sire, sired 7 Japanese Derby winners, and his last crop produced Irish-born Auguste Rodin, winner of the Derby and Irish Derby. His "impact" will carry on for generations.
